source.title: PAGnol: An Extra-Large French Generative Model
source.authors: Julien Launay; Elena Tommasone; B. Pannier; F. Boniface; A. Chatelain; Alessandro Cappelli; Iacopo Poli; Djamé Seddah

record.tranche_reason: Fits a compute-scaling law using the same power-law form and validation-loss measure as the cited work, on French models and data.
record.gate_note: The study fits a compute-versus-validation-loss law and reports validation perplexities across model sizes. It uses published scaling equations to choose training budgets but does not test whether the parameter/token allocation is compute-optimal, or whether small-run fits predict substantially larger runs. Downstream task scores are included for V6. Claims in the related-work section about other modalities and general downstream behavior are citations, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The authors fit Kaplan et al.'s compute power law (L = (k/C)^α, fit in log-log space under the efficient frontier) to the validation loss of French GPT models XXS–M and report their own exponent, α = −0.036. They also report validation perplexity and fine-tuned downstream scores across four model sizes. This is the original method and measure applied to a new language and dataset; T3 would also fit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The paraphrase should add two points. The authors interpret the smaller exponent as French being less compute-efficient than English, possibly due to its morphology and longer sentences. They also report that downstream fine-tuning performance improves with size but appears to saturate at XL, possibly due to a smaller fine-tuning batch size.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the same power-law form and compute/validation-loss relationship, but fits French PAGnol models trained on CCNet with a different codebase and hardware; L and XL are excluded from the fitted range.
record.method_sensitivity: Fit range and model setup matter to the reported fit: L and XL are excluded because of interrupted training and possible optimizer-state artifacts; XL also uses Rotary Embeddings. The authors note different datasets, codebase, and hardware from the English comparison.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
record.problems: The compute-law fit excludes L and XL, and no uncertainty for the exponent is reported. The French/English comparison is explicitly caveated by differing datasets, codebase, and hardware. Downstream scores are point results without reported uncertainty; some metrics flatten or decrease at larger sizes.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 5–8 report additional metrics for the same task conditions; only one primary metric per condition is recorded where the instructions permit. Prompt-tuning scores in Tables 9–11 are omitted to prioritize the pretraining scaling results and fine-tuned downstream results.

untested.parts: No separate laws in parameters or tokens. Data is fixed at 30GT, and size and compute co-vary across models.
No check of small-run fits against larger runs. L and XL are excluded, not predicted.
Kaplan's allocation is used to set budgets; the optimal split is not measured.
No shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Only text pretraining; other modalities, repeated data and transfer are untested.
No fitted relation between downstream scores and scale or loss; only four sizes.
No systematic variation of fitting choices, and no test of curve bending.

missing.what: Prompt-tuning scaling. Classification and OrangeSum scores rise with size, but FQuAD F1 falls from M to XL (0.561, 0.526, 0.450) while EM rises. The authors suspect a bug in their Rotary Embeddings prompt-tuning implementation.
Fitted constant k (3.40) and the compute range of the fit (about 1e-4 to 1e-1 PF-days) for the French compute law.

record.verdict_notes: V6 states were inconsistent across series and have been reassigned relative to the previous size in each series. The XL model differs in context length and positional embeddings, which confounds size comparisons at the top end. The V7 verdict rests on comparing the study's own exponent with a cited English value, with caveats the authors state explicitly.

versions.untested_parts: Tests compute scaling for French PAGnol models; it does not fit separate laws for parameter count or token count.
No evaluation of predictions from smaller runs against runs orders of magnitude larger.
Uses Kaplan et al.'s equations to choose budgets, but does not measure the loss-minimising parameter/token split or fit its trend.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No tests of other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as a pretraining scaling law.
Reports selected downstream task metrics across sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
Notes differences in data, code, hardware, interrupted training, and positional embeddings, but does not systematically vary fitting choices or test curve bending.

rows.operation_detail: Measured final validation perplexity after one epoch on 30GT of CCNet.
rows.note: Perplexity declines across the reported model-size sweep.
rows.check: A single point, not itself a power-law test. Across R1–R4, fr-wiki perplexity falls monotonically with size at fixed 30GT data. XL differs in context length (2048) and uses Rotary embeddings, so the XL step is confounded. The same caveat applies to R2–R8.

rows.subject: PAGnol XXS–M compute-law fit
rows.operation_detail: Fit the Kaplan et al. compute power-law form in log-log space, constrained below the efficient frontier; fit uses XXS, XS, S and M.
rows.locator: Section 4, “Scaling law for PAGnol models”; Figure 1
rows.note: The text compares this with −0.050 for English from cited work; that cited result is not separately recorded as a study result. L and XL were excluded because training interruptions could create curve artifacts and XL used Rotary Embeddings.
rows.check: The fitted constant (Figure 1: 3.40·C^-0.036) is not recorded. The fit covers about 1e-4 to 1e-1 PF-days, using XXS, XS, S and M only. No uncertainty is given.

relationships.reason: The study's own French exponent (−0.036) differs from English (−0.050). The authors attribute this to language, data, codebase and hardware, so the exponent depends on setup (R9).

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned FLUE, FQuAD and OrangeSum, sizes S to L (both OSCAR and CC-100 series)
relationships.reason: Scores rise with size on most tasks from S to M to L, and FQuAD F1 rises across all four sizes (R11, R13, R32, R38, R40–R45).
relationships.display_finding: Most scores improved from S to M for OSCAR and across tested S-to-L CC-100 models, and FQuAD F1 increased across all four sizes, although CC-100 OrangeSum ROUGE-1 declined from 28.20 to 28.12 between M and L.

source_check.condition: Fine-tuned FLUE, FQuAD and OrangeSum, sizes S to L (both OSCAR and CC-100 series)
source_check.reason: The directional-gain label is supported, but OSCAR has only S and M, not L. Restrict OSCAR to S→M and CC-100 to the tested S→L trends; CC-100 OrangeSum ROUGE-1 declines slightly from M=28.20 to L=28.12.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned FLUE at XL, and OrangeSum ROUGE-1 from M to L
relationships.reason: Gains stall or reverse: Books XL equals L, PAWS-X XL is below L, and other FLUE gains at XL are small. The authors confound this with a smaller fine-tuning batch size (R14, R15, R20, R21, R26, R27, R33, R39, R46).
relationships.display_finding: Books performance is unchanged from L to XL, PAWS-X declines, and other FLUE gains are small, with comparisons confounded by a smaller fine-tuning batch size.

tranche.reason: The study fits Kaplan's compute power-law form to validation loss using a log-log efficient-frontier fit.

source_check.notes: Tables and appendices label the main series CC-100, whereas the main text calls its pretraining data CCNet. Downstream evidence establishes directional trends without a fitted forecasting law; prompt-tuned FQuAD F1 is nonmonotonic, and the authors suspect an XL implementation bug.

reader_labels.reason: The authors fit the stated compute power-law form and report α = −0.036; the fit is limited to the reported range and setup (R9).

reader_labels.reason: FQuAD F1 rises across all four CC-100 sizes; most reported FLUE task scores also rise with size (R10–R43).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: FLUE and OrangeSum CC-100 comparisons at the largest sizes
reader_labels.reason: Some downstream scores saturate or decline at XL: Books does not improve from L, PAWS-X declines, and OrangeSum ROUGE-1 is slightly lower at L than M; the paper also reports prompt-tuning scaling slowing at XL (R14–R15, R32–R33, R46).
